svg.aria-label: Task 5.1 evaluation architecture, drawn as three phases flowing downward. Development and testing phase: evaluation datasets and rubrics - edge cases, adversarial inputs and regulatory boundaries curated as golden query-context-answer triples and version-controlled in Amazon S3 - feed Amazon Bedrock Evaluations, which offers LLM-as-a-Judge where a second model such as Claude 3 Opus scores the generator and never judges itself, Bring Your Own Inference for models hosted on Bedrock, SageMaker, EC2 or on-premises, and custom multi-dimensional scoring across relevance, factual accuracy, compliance and tone in parallel. CI/CD quality gates phase: AWS CodePipeline runs daily continuous evaluation orchestrated by AWS Step Functions, with the regression suite run against a fixed benchmark dataset so scores stay comparable between runs; a quality gate asks whether compliance is at or above 99.8 percent and accuracy at or above threshold. On a fail the release is blocked, triggering rollback and alert with no human discretion at deploy time. On a pass the change moves through shadow deployment, where real traffic is served and the output discarded, then canary deploy on a small percentage of live traffic, then full production with progressive scale-up on green metrics. Production monitoring phase: full production feeds two parallel streams. RAG and agent monitoring separates retrieve-only from retrieve-and-generate to isolate the vector search from the generator before blaming either, and tracks chunking, vector database health, citation precision and coverage, and Bedrock agent tool and reasoning evaluation. User feedback ingestion uses Kinesis Data Streams for live interactions at scale, SageMaker Ground Truth for expert review - the only tier that catches confident hallucinations and compliance gaps - and Amazon Comprehend for sentiment on open-text feedback. Both streams converge on Amazon QuickSight, providing role-based dashboards and trend analytics for engineering and business stakeholders.
